turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity pulling on Earth’s oceans, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, different coastlines move through areas of higher and lower water levels, creating high and low tides. Most places experience two high tides and two low tides each day, though patterns vary. Tides influence coastal ecosystems, navigation, fishing, and shoreline processes. Their timing and height can be predicted because they follow predictable astronomical cycles that repeat over time with remarkable natural regularity worldwide.
